newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. names envoy on plight of children in war zones.
newsitem.headline: U.N. names envoy on plight of children in war zones.

text.p: Olara Otunnu, a former Ugandan foreign minister, was appointed on Tuesday as the U.N. secretary-general's special representative on the impact of armed conflict on children.
The U.N. General Assembly last December recommended establishing the post to raise awareness of the plight of children in war zones and to help find ways of protecting them.

Otunnu, 46, was appointed for a three-year term. He is currently president of the International Peace Academy, a New York-based think tank that promotes the prevention and settlement of armed conflicts between and within states.

He was Uganda's U.N. representative from 1980 to 1985 and foreign minister in 1985. He has been mentioned in the past as a candidate for the post of U.N. secretary-general but is opposed by the government of Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni and is now a citizen of the Ivory Coast.
Otunnu is a graduate of Kampala's Makerere University, Oxford University and Harvard Law School.

In his new post he will build on the work of Graca Machel, widow of Mozambique's independence leader Samora Machel, who produced a groundbreaking study last year as a U.N. expert on the protection of children in armed conflicts.
Otunnu's appointment followed consultations with the U.N. High Commissioners for Refugees and for Human Rights and with the U.N. Children's Fund.
